transcript.text: Zanussi dishwasher keeps tripping the electrics, not every time though. Usually about 15 mins in. Model ZDT21006FA

A trip around 10–20 minutes into a cycle often points to a fault that appears when the dishwasher starts heating the water. On a Zanussi ZDT21006FA, common causes include:

• Heating element insulation fault – leakage to earth when it warms up; very common for an RCD trip.
• Water leak onto a component or wiring – sometimes only becomes apparent once circulation starts.
• Wash/circulation pump or drain pump fault.
• Damaged wiring, terminal, or mains interference filter.
• Less commonly, a faulty socket/circuit or a weak RCD/RCBO.

### First: don’t keep resetting it and running it
If it is tripping an RCD/RCBO (usually the switch marked “Test” or with 30 mA on it), it is detecting possible current leakage and should be treated as a safety issue. Turn the dishwasher off at its isolator/socket and leave it disconnected until checked.

### Safe checks you can do
1. Identify what trips
• A breaker marked B16/B32 etc. suggests overload/short circuit.
• A device with a Test button, often labelled RCD/RCBO, suggests earth leakage. A heater fault is especially likely in this case.

2. Check the plug/socket and supply
• With the appliance unplugged, inspect the plug, cable and socket for heat marks, damage, moisture or burning smell.
• Avoid using extension leads.
• If other appliances on the same circuit also cause issues, an electrician should check the circuit.

3. Look for obvious water evidence
• Pull the dishwasher out only if you can do so safely without straining hoses/cables.
• Check underneath and around the base for dampness, drips, white residue, or signs of a past leak.
• Check the door seal and the filter area inside for blockage, but do not dismantle electrical covers.

4. Note exactly when it trips
• If it fills and washes initially, then trips at about 15 minutes, tell the engineer this. It strongly helps diagnose a heater-related earth-leakage fault.

### Likely repair
An appliance engineer can insulation-test the heater and motors, and inspect for leaks. If the heater is faulty, it may be replaceable, though on some machines it is supplied as part of the sump/heater assembly.

Do not bypass the earth, use a higher-rated breaker, or repeatedly reset the RCD to finish a cycle. Arrange a dishwasher repair technician, or an electrician first if the socket/circuit itself appears suspect.
